fragmente.text: "Have you heard the legend? The black rose. They say it only grows by the lake. Whoever finds it, heals their heart. But it doesn't reveal itself to just anyone, and it isn't received lightly." Patrick closes his eyes for a moment. The words feel like a wound and a cure at once.

In Patrick Adams' office, the silence sits heavy, like an endless Sunday. On the corner of his desk stands an old photograph — a woman smiling with a rare stillness, as though her light touched everything around her. Her smile is meant for him, for a tomorrow life never brought.

"With treatment... maybe a year..." "No rounding up, Charles." "Six months. Maybe eight, with luck." A long, quiet murmur. Not resignation — a quiet, suppressed defiance. "So I've leased out the rest of my days. Splendid."

"I realized, standing by her grave, that I'd been living on the run. That I'd reduced love to a contract, and life to a set of statistics." "And now?" "Now I want to leave. To see the world through her eyes. Rome. Paris. London. I put it all off. There was no time. There was no courage. It's too late now for 'us' — but not for promises."

"Not everyone reaches the lake. And no one leaves it quite the way they arrived." "I'll take the risk." "It's not the path that's hard — it's what you carry inside you," the old man replies. "And know this: the clouds aren't your friends today. The storm comes down fast off that ridge."
I'm not running from fear. I'm running toward love. For her. For myself. Patrick doesn't look back. There's nothing left for him there. Everything that matters is ahead.
